top_choice_rationale: P002 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) honours a closed chain from a symmetry-based prediction (Z2 classification and protected helical edge states in time-reversal-invariant insulators) to its first experimental observation in HgTe wells, nearly two decades reproduced and conceptually far-reaching. The citation as slated is narrow enough to be defensible, and I read the 2016 prize as covering Chern-type and broken-time-reversal physics rather than Z2 insulators. The missing Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang credit is a real cost, but P001 (Katori, Ye) is a legitimate and cleanly attributed second choice. Both are clearly preferable to no award, since two mature candidates are available.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my work in string theory, quantum gravity and cosmology has no documented tie to Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Katori or Ye
